title: I Love You, Beth Cooper
full_review:
Though clearly targeted at teens, the comic misfire "I Love You, Beth Cooper" (Fox Atomic) features freewheeling sexual attitudes and behavior that make it unacceptable even for adults.

Director Chris Columbus' coming-of-age tale, adapted for the screen by Larry Doyle from his 2007 novel of the same title, chronicles a day -- and night -- in the life of nerdy high school graduate Denis Cooverman (Paul Rust). Urged on by his best friend and fellow outcast Rich (Jack T. Carpenter), Denis uses his speech as valedictorian to declare his long concealed love for head cheerleader Beth Cooper (Hayden Panettiere).

Embarrassed but touched, Beth accepts Denis' invitation to his graduation party, and arrives with her two closest pals from the pompom squad, Cammy (Lauren London) and Treece (Lauren Storm), in tow, only to discover that there are no other guests.

Denis and Rich make awkward attempts to entertain the trio, whom Denis refers to as "the trinity," until Beth's cocaine-addled ROTC boyfriend, Kevin (Shawn Roberts), appears, bent on wreaking vengeance. The new friends flee -- though not before Denis gets a thorough beating -- and take to the road with speed demon Beth behind the wheel.

Through the various adventures that follow, the unlikely pair bond. But their potentially charming relationship -- Denis genuinely cares for Beth's welfare, and urges her to live up to his idealistic image of her -- gets lost in the shuffle of well-worn social stereotypes, harshly violent confrontations with the implacable Kevin and the script's tacit approval of wayward sexuality.

Thus a recurring theme concerns Rich's sexual orientation, and his conflicted feelings about it, which are portrayed as needless and irrational. By contrast, Denis' outlook on his friend's situation -- which viewers are implicitly invited to share -- goes beyond loyalty and support to moral indifference.

A nude romp in the school showers and a bedroom scene involving one male and two female characters, though both take place off-screen, are likewise portrayed as no more than harmless fun.

The film contains brief nongraphic, nonmarital sexual activity, an off-screen three-way encounter, a benign view of group sex and homosexuality, underage drinking, drug references, much sexual and occasional irreverent humor, at least one use of the F-word, much crude language and a half-dozen uses of profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG-13 -- parents strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
